title: ReconFormer: Accelerated MRI Reconstruction Using Recurrent Transformer
grouping: Three equal panels in one row, unframed, captioned (a) 'Swin, PVT, etc.', (b) 'SwinIR, ViT, etc.', (c) 'ReconFormer (ours)'. Each repeats the same scene: the scan at the bottom, a layer stack above it, and a cloud-shaped call-out to the right holding the inside of the transformer layer.
shapes_depth: The brain MRI slice lies on a tilted perspective plane cut into a white grid of patches. Above it the layers are red-outlined transparent wireframe slabs - widening upward into a pyramid in (a), constant in (b) and (c) - joined to the image by a thin red vertical line. The call-out is a cloud outline reached by thick dashed black arrows; inside, tokens are small pale-blue parallelograms in perspective, attention is a translucent coloured quad between them, and FFN is a short upward arrow.
proposed_highlight: '(ours)' in the caption of (c); in (c) the attention sketch inside the cloud gains extra overlapping translucent coloured quads (several scales) where (a) and (b) show one.
lesson: Compare architectures by repeating one identical 3-D scene - the scan on a gridded patch plane, the layer stack above it, the attention sketch in a cloud call-out - and change only the stack's shape and the attention sketch between panels.
notes: elements 'other' = the wireframe layer stacks in perspective. Venue and year from Semantic Scholar (the arXiv PDF is set in the LNCS style).

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)
